data.source: same raw text subset of combined_corpus.txt, tokenized separately by each tokenizer

interpretation: SuperBPE was 7.9% worse (higher bits/byte = worse) at this tiny scale. SuperBPE's coarser tokenization yields ~12% fewer training tokens/gradient updates for the same raw text, and each token is a harder prediction target -- a disadvantage that likely outweighs the fragmentation benefit at this undertrained scale (9.4M params, ~4M words, 3 epochs). Consistent with the broader pattern that coarse tokenization schemes tend to show benefits at larger model/data scale. Treated as a genuine, reportable negative result, not a bug.
